back_translation: Do not let your mouth speak hastily, and do not let your heart rush to utter a word before God. For God dwells in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with many tasks, and the voice of a fool with many words.
When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, for He takes no pleasure in fools. What you have vowed, fulfill.
It is better not to vow at all than to vow and not fulfill it.
Do not let your mouth lead you into sin, and do not say before the messenger, “It was an unintentional slip.” Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
For many dreams bring what is without substance, and so do many words. Therefore, fear God.

If you see the oppression of the poor and the perversion of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one high official watches over another, and there are still higher ones over them.
The profit of the land belongs to all; even the king himself benefits from the fields.
He who loves money is never satisfied with money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied with income. This too is without substance.
When goods increase, those who eat them increase. What benefit then does the owner gain, except to look on with his eyes?
The sleep of the laborer is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the overfullness of the rich man does not allow him to sleep.
There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth that its owner hoarded until it became a danger to himself.
And that wealth perished in a failed venture, so when he has a son there is nothing left in his hand.
As he came from his mother's womb, so he will depart, naked as when he came. He can take nothing from his toil to carry away in his hand.
This too is a grievous evil: exactly as he came, so will he go. What gain does he get from toiling for the wind?
All his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and resentment.

Behold, what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat, to drink, and to enjoy what is good in all the toil at which one toils under the sun, throughout the few short days of life that God has given him — for this is his portion.
Moreover, every man to whom God has given riches and possessions, and whom He has empowered to eat of them, to receive his portion, and to rejoice in his toil — this is a gift from God.
For he will seldom reflect on the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
